artifacts.summary: Re-verifies all eleven confirmed phantom-declaration-citation instances, repairs the two that were not already fixed (plus adjacent phantom names found during that repair and five dead archive-path citations), and documents the new durable checker.

next_steps: Run /plan 728 to create an implementation plan, or treat this dispatch's direct repairs plus scripts/check-phantom-citations.sh as the completed deliverable and close the task -- no further Lean or engineering work is implied by the dispatch's HARD CONSTRAINTS (repair citations only, no Lean).

memory_candidates.content: When sweeping prose for phantom declaration citations, a shape-only backtick-span heuristic (dot/underscore/camelCase) over docs/**/*.md floods with false positives from namespaces/modules (no declaration keyword line to match -- add a namespace/directory/aggregator-file fallback), Lake build keywords (lean_exe/lean_lib), Lean linter/option roots (linter.*, synthInstance.*), and Mathlib/metaprogramming API names. A line-level co-occurrence gate (require a proof-engineering signal word like theorem/lemma/FormalSystem/.lean on the same source line) plus a namespace-root denylist cut a ~2200-candidate/685-finding first pass down to ~1000/105 on this repository. Also: a bash cache keyed by `grep "$needle" cache_file` is unsafe -- unrelated cached entries that merely contain $needle as a substring produce false cache hits; use an exact-match awk lookup instead.

In this repository, a task's own description text is a living document that accumulates dated correction paragraphs over time rather than being rewritten in place -- a prior revision may explicitly flag a phantom citation as unverifiable in an appended note while leaving the original citation uncorrected at its point of use (documented rationale: 'flagged rather than silently repaired because this revision was not scoped to re-derive the deliverable'). A later sweep should check for this specific pattern (flagged-but-not-fixed) rather than assuming an appended correction note means the citation itself was already handled.
